blocks.text: This chapter closes the Phase 1 report. It summarises the evidence, states what the evidence does not cover, lists the actions that remove these limits and draws the conclusion. Scenario numbers come from `docs/report/results_phase1.json` (generated 2026-10-23, MATLAB R2026b, Normal mode). Facts about the environment, the test suite and the open problems come from `docs/STATUS.md`.
Phase 1 evidence in brief

The Phase 1 set has nine scenarios with 71 pass/fail criteria, plus the free test drive D1, which has no criteria. **64 criteria pass, 6 fail and 1 is blocked** ({tab:tab_c_summary}). S0, S6c, S6d and S8a pass every criterion. S1 passes all 12 criteria it can evaluate. Its 13th criterion, the real-time-factor target, needs Accelerator mode and is blocked.

blocks.text: Limitations

The limitations fall into seven groups: simulation speed, blocked code generation, the open Phase 1 criteria, specification deviations, test-suite maintenance, functions that exist but were not exercised, and the physical assumptions of the model. Phase 2 is outside the scope of this report and is summarised only briefly.
Simulation speed and memory

items: All runs use Normal mode, because Windows Application Control blocks the Accelerator and Rapid Accelerator MEX files on the reference PC. The real-time factor (RTF, simulated time divided by execution time, compile excluded) is 0.31 to 0.55 for the flat-field runs and 0.134 for S2, the slope run with the full sprayer. One simulated second therefore costs 2-3 s of execution time, and about 7.5 s in S2 [TBD - cause of the low S2 RTF not analysed].

Each run also spends 0.5-2 min compiling and initialising the model before the first time step (wall time minus execution time: 33 s for S6d, 117 s for S0). Short scenarios are dominated by this overhead: S0 simulates 10 s in 148 s of wall time.

The `sim()` calls of the complete Phase 1 set, nine scenarios plus D1, took about 39 min of wall time (2315 s). The runs were made in two blocks on 2026-10-23 (result files written 07:25-07:56 and 20:11-20:47).
MATLAB memory grows with every compile of `Shaddad_System`, so long sessions must be split with a MATLAB restart in between ({sec:ch08_user_manual/PC requirements}).

The speed targets of decision D56 (S1 RTF ≥ 5, or ≥ 10 with MinGW-w64, the compiler now installed; S3 RTF ≥ 4; top model and every Model block accelerated) are not demonstrated. In the acceptance probe (`docs/STATUS.md` section 5.2) a 20 s S1 run with only the top model accelerated reached RTF 1.07, and its criteria matched Normal mode within 1e-4. That run was made during the acceptance (00:45-06:40), before the fix pass reported the Application Control block on the Accelerator MEX files (`docs/STATUS.md` section 0). Accelerating the Model blocks as well was not tried, and `run_scenario` currently sets the simulation mode of the top model only.
S3 (4 h endurance) has never been run. At Normal-mode speed it would take about 8 h of wall time.

blocks.text: Code generation and hardware builds
Simulink Coder is licensed but not installed. STM32CubeMX, STM32CubeCLT (with the GNU Tools for STM32) and STM32CubeProgrammer are missing. The consequences are:

items: No C code exists yet for `Shaddad_MCU` (STM32H743), `Shaddad_BMS` (STM32G474) or `Shaddad_Companion` (ROS 2). The three board builds of build task T17 report BLOCKED, and the 13 code-generation tests of the regression are Incomplete.

The hardware IO variants (`VC_TARGET` 1) are checked only by an update diagram. After the fix pass the BMS and Companion updates pass. The MCU update is blocked by the missing STM32CubeCLT, which supplies the device data of the register blocks.

The firmware has never run on its target. The MCU CPU load of 19.6 % is a design estimate (`build_targets('estimate')`), not a measurement, and the single-precision firmware has not yet been compared with generated code in SIL or PIL.

In simulation the MCU tasks execute in zero time on an ideal rate-monotonic schedule. The measured RC latencies (TX frame -> DRV_CMD 28 ms, stick -> ESC reference 50 ms) therefore contain no interrupt latency or execution-time jitter of the real MCU.

blocks.text: Open Phase 1 criteria

Six criteria fail and one is blocked ({tab:tab_c_open}). None of the failures is a missing safety function. Every commanded or required stop took place, ESTOP was entered only when commanded, and no BMS, ESC or MCU trip occurred. The failures are margin and calibration findings.

blocks.caption: Failed and blocked Phase 1 criteria
rows: MCU tilt estimate reached 26.3° (truth 23.7°), above the 22° warning. The class C derate halved the motor torque limit from 16 to 8 N m; the climb continued
Mean body pitch on the ramp is 2.2° steeper than the 20° ramp; this also feeds the tilt warning
The MCU controls track speed (0.800 m/s); the ground speed is lower because of about 7 % longitudinal slip
Short overshoot of the 100 ms moving-average deceleration over the 1.0 m/s² CTRL_STOP profile; the mean 90-10 % deceleration is 1.02 m/s²
0.9 % above the upper bound of the 2.0 m/s² ESTOP profile; peak 2.27 m/s² (≤ 2.4) and stop distance 0.59 m (≤ 0.7) pass
BLOCKED: Accelerator not available; Normal-mode RTF 0.47. The criterion text still says 'no C compiler', which is out of date

blocks.text: The S2 findings matter most for operation, because 20° with the full sprayer is the design slope, and on it the derate halves the available motor torque. Three observations explain the failures:

items: **Threshold.** The truth tilt itself reached 23.7°, above the 22° threshold. Even with a perfect estimate, the threshold leaves little or no margin above a 20° slope once the chassis pitch on its contact springs is added.

**Criterion.** T03 test T16 shows that the contact compliance alone adds 0.024 rad of pitch on a 20° slope (base robot, static; {sec:ch03_structure/Verification (Build Task T03)}). This accepted deviation already exceeds the ± 0.02 rad tolerance of S2.pitch, so the criterion and the accepted deviation contradict each other. The remaining part of the 0.039 rad offset with the 609 kg sprayer is not yet explained [TBD - T03 analysis].

**Estimator and speed definition.** The MCU estimate exceeded the truth tilt by a further 2.6° [TBD - fw_imu_tilt analysis]. The speed criterion is evaluated on ground speed, while the vehicle control closes the loop on track speed, so slip on the slope counts against it.

blocks.text: Several passing criteria have small margins. The hardware will add timing effects that the simulation does not contain, so these margins need to be re-measured on the target:

items: TX frame -> DRV_CMD 28 ms against 30 ms (S1).
CTRL_STOP 0.12 s after RF loss against 0.13 s (S6a).
RC age peak 92 ms against the 100 ms link-loss timeout at 1 % byte errors (S6c). The tolerable error rate between 1 % (link kept) and 5 % (link lost, S6d) has not been mapped.
HW_ESTOP fault bit 8 ms after the DI change against 11 ms (S8a).

blocks.text: Test suite

The full regression last ran during the acceptance, before the fix pass: 391 tests in 18 classes, of which 328 passed, 31 failed, 30 were incomplete and 2 were not run. It has not been re-run as a whole since. Of the 31 failures, 12 failed because the robot did not move (the two motion defects that the fix pass removed; S6c also because the SBUS decoder accepted corrupted frames). 3 are simulation-speed targets of the benches (two cached Normal-mode runs and the LoFi structure bench in Accelerator, RTF 67.5 against 100), 3 are known open problems (R2026b assertion, reference solver, `testD37_Latency`) and 13 are stale test expectations with no model defect behind them. Removing the motion defects does not make all 12 pass: a re-run would still fail tScenarios S2, S6a, S6b and S8b ({tab:tab_c_open}) and the Phase 2 scenarios S4, S5 and S7farm. The stale expectations are:

items: `t_infra` expects 87 bus objects (there are 88 since `Bus_TebMapCrop`) and one Solver Configuration (there are two since the Electronics_Thermal network). Its RC rate check also flags the Operator_RC instance block. Separately, the test does not retry after the R2026b `Stateflow:Assertion` on the first plant update.
`t_mcu_platform` still expects the T08 stubs that the T09 units replaced. `testD37_Latency` throws an exception with the real units.
`t_gnc_tracking` was written against the old MissionManager stub. The real FSM needs START (or `P.gnc.fsm.auto_start`) and geofence-safe rows.
`t_sensors` needs the base variable `sens_uavScene`, which exists only in a fresh session (Incomplete, not failed).
Model coverage is not collected, because Simulink Coverage is not installed.

blocks.text: Functions not exercised

items: **Dashboard driving** (`VC_OPSRC` 2). The variant compiles in the T-INT-10 variant matrix, but no drive with it has been verified. At RTF 0.3-0.5 the robot would respond in slow motion.
**Joystick input** (`VC_OPSRC` 3) is a placeholder. The `vrlib/Joystick Input` block failed its smoke test in R2026b, and Simulink 3D Animation is not installed.

**Test-drive options.** `phase1_test_drive` offers `Plan`, `EStopAt`/`ResetAt`, `RCLoss`, `World` and `Implement`, but `results_phase1.json` records only the default drive. The same functions are covered at scenario level by S8b, S6a and S2.
**Implements.** The only implement in the Phase 1 evidence is the full sprayer in S2. The mower appears only in the Phase 2 scenarios S3 and S4, and the tiller in no system scenario.
**Endurance and environment variants.** S3 (4 h) and the S7 variants S7wet and S7temp have never been run.

blocks.text: Model-fidelity assumptions
The digital twin is built from design data and physical first principles. {tab:tab_c_fidelity} lists the assumptions that bound how far the Phase 1 results carry over to the real robot.

blocks.caption: Model-fidelity assumptions and their effect on the Phase 1 results
rows: Averaged, non-switching models only: system-level Motor & Drive with loss maps and a 5 ms torque lag, averaged DC-DC converters (D56)
Currents and energy are mean values, with no PWM ripple, switching transients or EMC effects. The FOC plant with an average-value inverter is used on the bench only (T15)
ESC, motor, gearbox and implement-motor parameters are engineering estimates (risk R8)
The 16 N m torque envelope, the losses and the thermal time constants need supplier data
16S3P LFP pack from Battery Builder with 1-RC cells and no hysteresis (power spec risk R4)
SOC estimation on a real pack will be worse than in simulation
2-D Dahl/Janosi shear on 14 compliant contact points; steering factor and lateral friction from theory, not field data (risk R14); no radius-dependent turning resistance
Slip (about 7 % in S2), yaw response and stop distances rest on soil parameters that are not validated
Fixed DEM on a 0.25 m grid with five soil classes; Phase 1 uses the flat test field (world 1) and one 20° ramp (world 2); outside the DEM the ground continues flat
No rough ground, side slopes, berms or wet soil in the Phase 1 evidence
Collisions are detected but exert no forces; tank slosh, implement compliance, track tension and derailment are not modelled
'0 collisions' is a clearance check, not a crash simulation
Precharge resistor 4.7 Ω instead of 22 Ω (`P.sim.ovr.R_pre`); initial-condition workaround for `Electronics_Plant/DI_Latency` (`scn_ic_elec_hw`)
S0 power-up timing holds only with the override. With 22 Ω the ESC idle load holds the bus at 87 % of V_pack and HV_Ready never rises
Fixed-step ode3 at 1 ms with local Simscape solvers; the reference-solver mode fails (open problem 12)
No reference run bounds the fixed-step error; the energy-audit residuals (at most 4.4e-5 in S1) are the main accuracy evidence
All Phase 1 runs use the defaults: HiFi chassis, SYS motor plant, grouped pack
The LoFi, IDEAL and lumped variants are verified on benches only

blocks.text: **Result provenance.** S1, S6c, S6d and S8a come from post-fix result files written between 07:25 and 07:56 on 2026-10-23 and were not re-run for this report. D1, S0, S2, S6a, S6b and S8b were re-run between 20:11 and 20:47. According to `docs/STATUS.md` section 0 and the file time stamps, the later model changes concern the hardware IO variants (`VC_TARGET` 1), which the SIM runs do not use. The S6 and S8 scoring fixes were in place before the S6c, S6d and S8a runs.
Phase 2 status

Phase 2 is outside this report; {sec:ch07_phase2_preview/Current Status} gives the status of S4, S5 and S7. The open items are policy and tuning issues in the GNC, perception and navigation units. They do not affect the Phase 1 chain, which runs with the GNC stub.
Recommendations

{tab:tab_c_reco} lists the recommended actions. **High** priority means the item blocks hardware work, a phase gate or the credibility of a design value. **Medium** means it closes an open Phase 1 finding. **Low** means it improves the tooling. The table suggests the domain that leads each item. Named owners and deadlines are to be set at the Phase 1 review [TBD - Phase 1 review].

blocks.text: Details of R1, R3, R4, R12 and R13:

items: **R1.** Run `build_targets('products')`, `shaddad_configsets('codegen')`, `build_targets('preflight')` and the three T17 board builds (`build_targets()`), as listed in the command block at the end of this section. Acceptance: MCU CPU estimate < 50 %, flash < 1 MB.

**R3.** D56 targets: S1 RTF ≥ 5 (≥ 10 with MinGW-w64) and S3 RTF ≥ 4. Stale texts: the S1.rtf criterion ('no C compiler'), the `run_scenario` help ('none is installed') and the `phase1_test_drive` header (about 62 s and 2-3 min; measured 64 s and about 4-5 min).

**R4.** Decide with the safety owner how TILT_WARN (22°) relates to the 20° design slope, reduce the 2.6° tilt-estimate error (`fw_imu_tilt`), base S2.pitch on the compliance-including reference with the sprayer mass, and define S2.v_mean on track speed or with a slip allowance.

**R12.** Bring-up order: MCU on the NUCLEO-H743ZI2, SBUS test T-EL-43, PIL timing T-EL-42 with the Execution Profiler, BMS board, CAN1 drives, then the vehicle with the tracks off the ground. HIL rig for the MCU against the simulated plant: [TBD - rig and real-time target].

**R13.** Data needed: slip and turning per soil class (steering factor, lateral friction, 20° ramp with the sprayer), motor and ESC supplier data, pack capacity, resistance and hysteresis, and the mass and CG of each implement.

blocks.text: Suggested sequence

items: **Tooling (R1, R2).** These two items unblock most of the remaining work and need no model change.
**Phase 1 closure (R3-R9, R15).** Close the six open criteria, settle the specification conflicts, update the tests and issue a closure revision of this report.
**Hardware path (R12-R14).** Bring up the boards and validate the plant in the field, then update the parameters and re-run S0-S8 on the updated model.
**Phase 2 (R10, R11, R16).** This work can run in parallel with the hardware path, because it mainly touches the companion units and the tooling.

blocks.text: Once R1 and R2 are done, run these checks in a fresh MATLAB session (`run_scenario` and `run_regression` are described in {sec:ch08_user_manual/Running the predefined scenarios} and {sec:ch08_user_manual/Running tests}):

openProject('<project root>\Shaddad_UGV.prj');
S   = build_targets('products')       % must list nothing missing
shaddad_configsets('codegen');          % complete the code-generation sets
F   = build_targets('preflight')      % fresh process, VC_TARGET 1 (5-20 min)
rep = build_targets()                 % MCU, BMS and Companion board builds
r1a = run_scenario('S1', 'Mode', 'accelerator', 'StopTime', 20)   % top-model Accelerator check
rt  = run_regression('Fast')          % Fast-tagged static checks and unit benches, about 1-3 min
Conclusions

**Phase 1 of the Shaddad digital twin is demonstrated.** The model runs the complete remote-control chain in one closed loop. The simulated transmitter sends SBUS frames over the UART line model. The STM32H743 firmware model decodes and maps them, and its mode manager and vehicle control turn them into DRV_CMD frames on CAN1. The two ESC models then drive the PMSM, gearbox and track networks on the soil model, powered by the 48 V LFP pack under the BMS and the hard-wired safety chain. Across the nine Phase 1 scenarios 64 of 71 criteria pass, and S0, S6c, S6d and S8a pass in full. S1 meets every criterion it can evaluate: 90 % speed rise in 1.51 s, a steady speed error of 0.0072 m/s, a yaw-rate tracking error of 4.9 %, 28 ms from TX frame to DRV_CMD, 50 ms from stick to ESC reference, and a stop from 1.2 m/s within 0.844 m. The safety functions behave as specified. The SBUS decoder filters 1 % byte errors without a channel glitch. A 5 % error rate, an RF loss or a silent SBUS line leads to a controlled stop without a false ESTOP. The front E-stop removes torque within 15 ms and stops the robot within 0.213 m, and the robot drives again only after reset and re-arm. In the default test drive the robot covers 34.8 m, follows the commanded speed and yaw rate within about 0.025 m/s and 0.011 rad/s, and rejects no SBUS frame.

The remaining findings concern margins rather than missing functions. On the 20° design slope the tilt threshold, the tilt estimate and two criteria do not yet agree with the physics, and the stop profiles exceed their deceleration limits by 0.9 to 9.7 %. The twin is therefore ready to serve as the desktop reference for the Phase 1 control and safety logic and as the base for the Phase 2 work. It is not yet a real-time or hardware tool: Normal mode runs at 0.13 to 0.55 times real time, code generation and board builds are blocked by missing tools, and the plant parameters rest on design estimates rather than field data. Recommendations R1, R2, R4, R6 and R12-R14 turn the Phase 1 model into a validated basis for the first Shaddad hardware.
